content:
DrorPay sends HTTP POST requests to your configured payment_callback_url for payment lifecycle events.

Events sent:
- payment.created: Intent was created (status: pending)
- payment.completed: Payment succeeded (status: completed)
- payment.failed: Payment failed (status: failed)
- payment.cancelled: Payment was cancelled (status: cancelled)
- payment.test: Sent by POST /admin/platform/test-webhook for integration testing

All webhook payloads include: event, platform_transaction_id, platform_order_id, status, amount, fee_paid, platform_charges, timestamp, additional_data.

Webhooks are your primary backup for socket events. Implement idempotency — you may receive duplicate notifications from both socket and webhook channels for the same event.

Webhook retry behavior:
- Retry attempts: up to 3
- Retry delays: 2s, 4s, 8s (exponential backoff)
- Success criteria: HTTP 2xx response from your endpoint
- No retry on HTTP 4xx (DrorPay treats 4xx as client-side misconfiguration)
- Timeout per attempt: 30 seconds

Best practice: return HTTP 200 immediately and process the event asynchronously. Long synchronous processing risks hitting the 30-second timeout, which triggers retries.

If your endpoint is down during all retry attempts, use the polling endpoint GET /platform/v1/transaction-details/:id to recover the final transaction state.

Test webhook integration (admin only): POST /admin/platform/test-webhook

Request body: { "platformId": "<uuid>" }

DrorPay sends a test payload with event 'payment.test' to your configured payment_callback_url.

Response:
{ "success": true, "status_code": 200, "response_data": {}, "webhook_url": "...", "timestamp": "..." }

Use this during development to:
- Confirm your endpoint is publicly reachable
- Verify your payload parsing works correctly
- Test your signature verification logic

The test payload includes: event, platform_transaction_id ('test-transaction-id'), platform_order_id ('test-order-id'), status ('test'), amount (100.00), and additional_data.test: true.
